role: Second step of the assistant's destructive actions: AssistantActionConfirmations holds at most one pending request and confirms it only when the user's next message is an explicit yes (AffirmationReply); requests lapse after another turn or 10 minutes.
types: PendingAssistantAction: struct Equatable Sendable — action key, lowercased target, requesting user turn id, time
AssistantActionConfirmations: final class (@MainActor) — pending-request store; Outcome enum confirmed/awaitingConfirmation/noUserMessage
AffirmationReply: enum — explicit-yes classifier over word lists in the shipped languages
state: mem:AffirmationReply.affirmations (Set<String>, no duplicates — a duplicate traps)
toplevel: Type declarations and static constants only.

units.does: Nonisolated empty initializer (pending starts nil), so the shared instance and a test case can each build one.
units.entry: AssistantActionConfirmations.shared (read only by AppDependencies AssistantServices.assistantActionConfirmations) and tests

units.does: Filters the transcript to user turns. With none, clears pending and returns .noUserMessage. Lowercases target; if confirms() holds, clears pending and returns .confirmed; otherwise records PendingAssistantAction(action, target, latest user turn id, now) — replacing any earlier request — and returns .awaitingConfirmation.

branches.cond: no user turn in the transcript

branches.effect: pending=nil, returns .confirmed; else records the request and returns .awaitingConfirmation

units.does: True only when a pending request has the same action and target, is at most `lifetime` (10 min) old, was recorded during the user turn directly before the latest one, and the latest user turn is an explicit yes (AffirmationReply.isExplicitYes).

branches.cond: no pending, different action/target, expired, fewer than two user turns, or the request was not made during the previous user turn
branches.effect: returns false; else returns isExplicitYes(latest text)

units.does: Tokenizes the reply; true when it has 1-5 words, none of them a negation/hedge (no, not, don, but, wait, cancel, nein, nicht, non, pas, … in the shipped languages) and the first word or two-word opening is an affirmation (yes, ok, sure, do it, go ahead, ja, oui, d accord, sí, sì, да, はい, 네, 是的, …).

branches.cond: empty or more than maxWords (5) words
first word or two-word opening is an affirmation

units.does: Lowercases and splits on whitespace, punctuation and symbols, dropping empty pieces ("d'accord" → ["d","accord"]).
